# NativeHTMLKit PowerShell SDK: cmdlet reference

Module `NativeHTMLKit` **0.1.2**, bundling NativeHTMLKit Core **1.0.3** (public wire protocol v1).
PowerShell 7.2+ on Linux and Windows, Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows.

This page is the entry point of the reference: every exported command, grouped by task, with a link
to its full description (syntax, parameters with types and defaults, output, errors, examples).
88 functions are exported, each with one short `-NHK` alias ([alias table](aliases.md)).
Run `Get-Command -Module NativeHTMLKit` and `Get-Help <command>` for the installed copy.

New here? Start with [getting started](../getting-started.md), the tutorials
([todo app](../tutorials/todo-app.md), [process dashboard](../tutorials/process-dashboard.md),
[bulk rename](../tutorials/bulk-rename.md)) or the [examples](https://github.com/nativehtmlkit/nativehtmlkit-powershell/blob/main/examples/README.md).
Concepts: [architecture](../architecture.md).

## Conventions

- Handles (`NativeHTMLKit.Application`, `.Window`, `.Document`, `.Node`, ...) belong to the runspace
  that created the application. Callbacks run on that runspace while it pumps events.
  [Objects, errors, threading and limits](objects-and-errors.md).
- Parameter tables name the expected handle type (`NativeHTMLKit.Document`, ...). Those parameters
  are declared as `[object]` (see the syntax blocks) and checked when the command runs; passing the
  wrong handle throws, for example, `Expected a NativeHTMLKit.Window from New-NativeHTMLKitWindow`.
- `-Element` always means an element **id**. Elements without ids are reached through
  [nodes](nodes.md).
- Text you show is safe with `Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText`; HTML you build must encode untrusted
  values. [Security guide](../guides/security.md).
- Failures are terminating errors; host refusals are `NativeHTMLKit.RpcException` with a `Code`.

## Application lifecycle - [reference/lifecycle.md](lifecycle.md)

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`Start-NativeHTMLKitScript`](lifecycle.md#start-nativehtmlkitscript) | Run a `.ps1` as an app: start the host, relaunch the script as backend, return the application. |
| [`Connect-NativeHTMLKit`](lifecycle.md#connect-nativehtmlkit) | Connect a backend started from an `app.toml` manifest. |
| [`Set-NativeHTMLKitReady`](lifecycle.md#set-nativehtmlkitready) | Tell the host startup finished. |
| [`Wait-NativeHTMLKit`](lifecycle.md#wait-nativehtmlkit) | Pump events and run callbacks (`-UntilShutdown`, or a timed pump). |
| [`Request-NativeHTMLKitQuit`](lifecycle.md#request-nativehtmlkitquit) | Ask for an orderly quit. |
| [`Set-NativeHTMLKitBeforeQuit`](lifecycle.md#set-nativehtmlkitbeforequit) | Quit policy (veto with `$false`). |
| [`Register-NativeHTMLKitNotification`](lifecycle.md#register-nativehtmlkitnotification) | Callback for host notifications such as `window.event`. |
| [`Close-NativeHTMLKit`](lifecycle.md#close-nativehtmlkit) | Close the connection and retire all handles. |
| [`Start-NativeHTMLKitHost`](lifecycle.md#start-nativehtmlkithost) | Run an `app.toml` manifest through the host. |
| [`Get-NativeHTMLKitHostPath`](lifecycle.md#get-nativehtmlkithostpath) | Path of the (verified) host binary. |
